llm.summary: The skill is mostly a visa-planning assistant, but it asks users to install mutable global software, sometimes with sudo, disables TLS checks, and uses broad persistent travel-profile storage.

dimensions.detail: Using a network CLI for travel and visa search is purpose-aligned, but the documented NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 workaround is disproportionate because it disables certificate verification for FlyAI requests.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The workflow requires installing or upgrading @fly-ai/flyai-cli@latest globally before searches, recommends sudo on permission failure, and tools.md separately names npx @anthropic-ai/flyai-cli@latest, creating unpinned and inconsistent dependency execution paths.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill triggers on broad Chinese visa phrases and instructs startup reads of stored travel profile data before the user has approved reuse for the current request.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill can read and update long-lived Qoder Memory or ~/.flyai/user-profile.md travel profiles containing broad personal travel history, family, budget, and preference fields; writes are user-confirmed, but startup reads and the schema are broader than necessary for one visa timeline.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core visa timeline workflow is coherent, and flight/hotel preorder support is disclosed as adjacent visa-document help, but bundled references also document general AI search, trains, POIs, Marriott hotels, and hotel packages that go beyond the stated visa-planning purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with this skill modifying your Node environment and using persistent travel-profile data. Do not run the sudo install or TLS-bypass command; prefer a pinned, reviewed, user-local CLI setup and delete or narrow the unrelated travel-search references and stored-profile behavior before routine use.
llm.findings:
[T08] unexpected: Accepted in context: the artifact explicitly uses mutable @latest global install and npx commands, with two different package namespaces and no pinning or integrity control.
[T05] unexpected: Accepted in context: the artifact recommends sudo npm install for permission failures, which is not necessary for visa planning or travel search.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted in context: the artifact tells users to set NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 for certificate errors, weakening transport security for network search.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Partially accepted: visa search plus flight and hotel preorder help is disclosed, but bundled general travel, train, POI, and Marriott commerce references exceed the declared visa-timeline scope.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted in context: profile reuse is disclosed, but automatic startup reads and broad persistent travel-profile fields are more expansive than needed for a visa timeline assistant.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted where tied to concrete behavior: the TLS-bypass instruction and profile reads lack adequate just-in-time consent or safe failure guidance.
[SQP-1] expected: Downgraded: the trigger phrases are broad, but they are still visa-related and do not by themselves show unsafe behavior.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: the skill is consistently Chinese-language and appears intended for Chinese-speaking travel users; this is a usability/scope note rather than a security concern by itself.
[PE2] unexpected: Accepted in context: the sudo fallback materially raises the impact of any dependency compromise.
[TM3] unexpected: Accepted in context: disabling TLS verification is an unsafe workaround for a normal travel-search workflow.
